Murtaugh's smoked trout dip and crackers
the fishing trip on Roger's boat

Hot-smoked trout flaked into cream cheese with lemon, dill and horseradish, topped with capers and served with crisp water crackers. Remove the skin and bones from 200g hot-smoked trout and flake it. Beat 200g softened cream cheese with 2 tbsp sour cream, the zest and juice of half a lemon, 2 tsp horseradish and 2 tbsp chopped dill. Fold the trout through, keeping some chunks, and season with pepper. Spoon into a bowl, scatter with 1 tbsp capers and extra dill, and serve with water crackers.

Wonton wrappers cut in triangles, fried at 180C until puffed, tossed in salt and five spice, sweet chilli dip.
M: Chinatown, where Uncle Benny runs things
Duck pricked, dried overnight, rubbed with five spice and salt inside, roasted at 180C for 90 minutes, glazed with honey and soy for the last 15. Pancakes, cucumber and hoisin.
a fishing boat should mean fish for dinner

Whole snapper scored and stuffed with lemon, garlic and herbs, grilled over hot coals until the skin blisters, with charred lemon and garlic butter. Score 2 whole snapper (about 800g each) three times on each side, rub with oil and salt, and stuff with lemon slices, 2 sliced garlic cloves, parsley and dill. Grill over medium-hot coals or a barbecue for 8 to 10 minutes a side until the flesh flakes at the bone. Grill 2 halved lemons cut side down. Melt 60g butter with 1 crushed garlic clove and chopped parsley and spoon over the fish.

K: Chinatown, where Uncle Benny runs things

Gin and lychee syrup over ice, topped with spicy ginger ale and lime, garnished with a whole lychee and a sliver of fresh ginger. Drain a 565g tin of lychees, keeping the syrup. Fill 4 highball glasses with ice. Add 45ml gin and 30ml lychee syrup to each, plus a squeeze of lime. Top with 150ml cold ginger ale and stir once. Thread a lychee onto a cocktail pick with a thin slice of fresh ginger and lay it across each glass.

s.how: Mix 300g pork mince, 150g chopped prawns, 3 chopped shiitake, 1 tbsp grated ginger and 1 tbsp soy. Spoon into 24 wonton wrappers, pinch up the sides leaving the top open and add a dot of grated carrot. Steam for 8 minutes.

s.note: Leo's back, and he will not stop talking
s.how: Cut 20 wonton wrappers into triangles. Fry at 180C in batches for about 30 seconds until puffed and golden. Drain and toss with salt and a pinch of five spice. Serve with sweet chilli sauce for dipping.

m.note: Chinatown, where Uncle Benny runs things
m.how: Prick a 2kg duck all over and dry uncovered in the fridge overnight. Rub inside with five spice and salt. Roast at 180C for 90 minutes, glazing with 2 tbsp honey and 2 tbsp soy for the last 15. Serve with 20 pancakes, cucumber, spring onion and hoisin.

w.note: Leo talks too much, his fortune says so
w.how: Whisk 3 egg whites with 100g sugar, then stir in 60g flour, 40g melted butter and a little vanilla. Spread 8cm circles on a lined tray and bake at 180C for 6 minutes. Working fast, fold each around a paper fortune.

d.note: Chinatown, where Uncle Benny runs things
